questions.q: Two closed $n$-manifolds $M_0,M_1$ are cobordant when there exists a compact $(n+1)$-manifold $W$ with what boundary?
questions.explain: The cobordism relation requires $\partial W = M_0 \sqcup M_1$ — disjoint union, with $W$ filling between the two ends. This makes the relation transitive: glue two cobordisms along the shared end.

questions.q: Which of these closed manifolds are null-cobordant in the unoriented bordism ring $\Omega_*^{O}$? Select all that apply.
questions.explain: Closed orientable surfaces bound handlebodies. Spheres bound disks. $\mathbb{RP}^3 = SO(3)$ is the boundary of the disk bundle of the tautological line bundle on $\mathbb{RP}^2$ (or argued via SW numbers — they all vanish on $\mathbb{RP}^3$). $\mathbb{RP}^2$ is the canonical non-trivial example: $w_1(T\mathbb{RP}^2)^2 \ne 0$ in $H^*(\mathbb{RP}^2;\mathbb{Z}/2)$, so $\mathbb{RP}^2$ generates $\Omega_2^{O} = \mathbb{Z}/2$ and is not null-cobordant.

questions.q: What is the order of $\Omega_2^{O}$, the unoriented bordism group of closed surfaces?
questions.explain: $\Omega_2^{O} \cong \mathbb{Z}/2$, generated by $[\mathbb{RP}^2]$. Every other closed surface (orientable $\Sigma_g$, Klein bottle, higher non-orientable surfaces) is either null-cobordant or cobordant to $\mathbb{RP}^2$.

cob-numbers.title: Stiefel–Whitney and Pontryagin numbers as obstructions

questions.q: Thom's theorem (1954) states that a closed manifold $M^n$ is null-cobordant in $\Omega_*^{O}$ if and only if:
choices: Every Stiefel–Whitney number of $M$ vanishes in $\mathbb{Z}/2$
questions.explain: The complete list of obstructions to null-cobordism in $\Omega_*^{O}$ is the family of Stiefel–Whitney numbers $\langle w_{i_1}\smile\cdots\smile w_{i_r}(TM),[M]\rangle$ ranging over all monomials of total degree $n$. They are simultaneously cobordism invariants and a complete invariant.

questions.q: For oriented bordism $\Omega_*^{SO}$, which characteristic numbers serve as obstructions?
questions.explain: A closed oriented $M$ is null-cobordant in $\Omega_*^{SO}$ iff every Stiefel–Whitney number AND every Pontryagin number vanishes. Pontryagin numbers alone do not detect 2-torsion in $\Omega_*^{SO}$.

questions.q: Let $M = \mathbb{RP}^2$. The Stiefel–Whitney number $\langle w_1(T\mathbb{RP}^2)^2,[\mathbb{RP}^2]\rangle$ in $\mathbb{Z}/2$ equals what value? (Enter $0$ or $1$.)
questions.explain: $H^*(\mathbb{RP}^2;\mathbb{Z}/2)=\mathbb{Z}/2[a]/(a^3)$ with $|a|=1$, and $w(T\mathbb{RP}^2)=(1+a)^3=1+a+a^2$. So $w_1=a$, $w_1^2=a^2$, and $\langle a^2,[\mathbb{RP}^2]\rangle=1$. This non-vanishing is exactly what shows $[\mathbb{RP}^2]\ne 0$ in $\Omega_2^{O}$.

cob-thom.title: Thom's theorem and the Thom spectrum

questions.q: The Pontryagin–Thom construction identifies the unoriented bordism ring with which homotopy invariant?
choices: $\Omega_*^{O}\cong\pi_*(MO)$, the homotopy groups of the Thom spectrum
questions.explain: The Pontryagin–Thom construction is an isomorphism $\Omega_n^{O}\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi_n(MO)$, where $MO$ is the Thom spectrum of the universal bundle on $BO$. It converts a manifold-classification problem into a stable-homotopy computation.

questions.q: Thom's calculation $\pi_*(MO)=\mathbb{F}_2[x_i : i\ne 2^k-1]$ has polynomial generators in which degrees? Pick the smallest five.
questions.explain: We exclude $i = 2^k-1 = 1,3,7,15,\ldots$. The smallest allowed degrees are $2,4,5,6,8,9,10,11,12,13,14,16,\ldots$. The first five are $2,4,5,6,8$.

questions.q: What is the order (as an abelian group) of $\Omega_4^{O}$? Use Thom's calculation: $\Omega_*^{O}=\mathbb{F}_2[x_2,x_4,x_5,x_6,\ldots]$.
questions.explain: In degree 4, the monomials of total degree 4 in $\mathbb{F}_2[x_2,x_4,x_5,\ldots]$ are $x_2^2$ and $x_4$. So $\Omega_4^{O}\cong\mathbb{F}_2\oplus\mathbb{F}_2\cong(\mathbb{Z}/2)^2$, of order $4$.

cob-oriented.title: Oriented cobordism and the signature theorem

questions.q: What does Hirzebruch's signature theorem assert for a closed oriented $4k$-manifold $M$?
choices: $\sigma(M) = \langle L_k(p_1,\ldots,p_k),[M]\rangle$, where $L_k$ is the $L$-genus polynomial in Pontryagin classes
$\sigma(M)$ equals the index of the Dirac operator
questions.explain: The Hirzebruch signature theorem expresses the signature as a characteristic number: $\sigma(M)=\langle L_k(p_1,\ldots,p_k),[M]\rangle$, with $L_1 = p_1/3$ and $L_2 = (7p_2-p_1^2)/45$. So the signature ring map $\Omega_*^{SO}\to\mathbb{Z}$ is computed entirely from Pontryagin numbers.

questions.q: Rationally, $\Omega_*^{SO}\otimes\mathbb{Q}$ is a polynomial ring on which generators?
questions.explain: $\Omega_*^{SO}\otimes\mathbb{Q}\cong\mathbb{Q}[\mathbb{CP}^2,\mathbb{CP}^4,\mathbb{CP}^6,\ldots]$. Odd-complex-dimensional $\mathbb{CP}^{2k+1}$ are null-cobordant orientedly (their $L$-genus vanishes), so only even ones survive.

questions.q: Compute $\sigma(\mathbb{CP}^2)$, the signature of the complex projective plane.
questions.explain: $H^2(\mathbb{CP}^2;\mathbb{Z})=\mathbb{Z}\cdot x$ with intersection form $\langle x\smile x,[\mathbb{CP}^2]\rangle = 1$. The form $(1)$ is positive definite of rank one, so $\sigma(\mathbb{CP}^2)=1$. Equivalently, $L_1(p_1)=p_1/3$ paired against $[\mathbb{CP}^2]$: $p_1(T\mathbb{CP}^2)=3x^2$, giving $\sigma=1$.

questions.q: Surgery on an embedded $S^p\times D^q\hookrightarrow M^{p+q}$ replaces the embedded piece with what?
choices: $D^{p+1}\times S^{q-1}$, glued along the common boundary $S^p\times S^{q-1}$
questions.explain: $S^p\times D^q$ and $D^{p+1}\times S^{q-1}$ both have boundary $S^p\times S^{q-1}$. Surgery removes the first and glues in the second, producing a new manifold of the same dimension; the trace of the operation is a cobordism between the old and new manifolds.

questions.q: Smale's $h$-cobordism theorem applies under which hypotheses?
choices: Any cobordism between any two manifolds is trivial
$\dim M\ge 5$ and $M_0,M_1$ simply connected, $W$ an $h$-cobordism — then $W\cong M_0\times[0,1]$
$M$ orientable and compact — without any dimension or $\pi_1$ hypothesis
questions.explain: Smale's theorem requires $\dim M\ge 5$ AND simple connectivity. Both hypotheses are essential: in dimension $4$ the theorem fails (Donaldson, Freedman), and without simple connectivity the Whitehead torsion $\tau(W)\in\mathrm{Wh}(\pi_1)$ obstructs (the $s$-cobordism theorem).

questions.q: What does the $h$-cobordism theorem imply about the smooth Poincaré conjecture in dimension $\ge 6$?
choices: Any homotopy $n$-sphere ($n\ge 6$) is homeomorphic — and indeed PL-homeomorphic — to $S^n$
questions.explain: Smale used $h$-cobordism to prove the Poincaré conjecture in dimensions $\ge 5$ (in the topological/PL category): any homotopy $n$-sphere is homeomorphic to $S^n$. (Smooth uniqueness fails: Milnor's exotic $7$-spheres are homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic to $S^7$.)

questions.q: Atiyah's axioms describe a $d$-dimensional TQFT as:
choices: A Hodge structure on cobordism classes
questions.explain: Atiyah's TQFT is a symmetric monoidal functor: closed $(d-1)$-manifolds go to vector spaces, cobordisms go to linear maps, disjoint union goes to tensor product, and the empty manifold goes to the ground field $k$.

questions.q: If $Z\colon\mathrm{Cob}_d\to\mathrm{Vect}_k$ is a TQFT and $M$ is a closed $d$-manifold (regarded as a morphism $\emptyset\to\emptyset$), what is $Z(M)$?
choices: A vector space — the state space of $M$
An element of $k$ — the partition function of $M$
questions.explain: $\emptyset$ is the monoidal unit, so $Z(\emptyset)=k$. A cobordism $\emptyset\to\emptyset$ produces a linear map $k\to k$, i.e. multiplication by a scalar — the partition function $Z(M)\in k$.

questions.q: The Baez–Dolan / Lurie cobordism hypothesis says that a fully extended framed $d$-TQFT valued in a symmetric monoidal $(\infty,d)$-category $\mathcal{C}$ is determined by:
choices: Its value on the empty manifold
Its values on all closed $d$-manifolds simultaneously
Its value on a single point — and that value can be any fully dualizable object of $\mathcal{C}$
Its restriction to the subcategory of orientable cobordisms
questions.explain: The cobordism hypothesis: extended framed $d$-TQFTs $\mathrm{Bord}_d^{fr}\to\mathcal{C}$ are equivalent to fully dualizable objects of $\mathcal{C}$, via $Z\mapsto Z(\mathrm{pt})$. Adding tangential structure (orientation, spin, ...) corresponds to taking homotopy fixed points under an $O(d)$-action.
